title: Graphene Coatings for Biomedical Implants
protocol: Graphene-coat NiTi substrates using chemical vapor deposition.
Place Cu foils in a quartz tube furnace and heat to 1,000 °C under H2 and Ar flow.
Introduce methane into the furnace for 20-30 min at different flow rates.
Cool samples to room temperature under flowing H2, Ar, and CH4.
Spin-coat Cu foils with PMMA diluted in anisole at 4,000 rpm followed by heat treatment at 150 °C.
Etch Cu foil using CE-100 etchant and rinse in 10% HCl and de-ionized water for 10 min.
Transfer graphene attached to the PMMA layer onto NiTi substrates (4.5 mm2).
Anneal samples at 450 °C under Ar and H2 flow for 2 hours to remove PMMA.
Wash final substrate with acetone to dissolve residual PMMA.
Use a Dilor XY triple grating monochromator for micro-Raman characterization of Gr-NiTi samples using a 100X objective and 514.5 nm excitation from an Ar+ ion laser.
Culture rat aortic endothelial cells on gelatin-coated 8 chambers slides.
Place pristine and Gr-NiTi substrates in wells without any gelatin coating for cell growth testing.
Grow rat aortic smooth muscle cells as control group in CellBind 96-well plates in Dulbecco's Modified Eagle Medium.
Seed cells (both endothelial and smooth muscle cells) at 10^5 cells/well in wells containing pristine NiTi, 1 sccm or 4 sccm Gr-NiTi substrates.
Grow cells for the desired time period in an incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO2, exchanging media every other day.
Remove media at the end time point and add fresh media containing 0.5 mg/ml thiazolyl blue tetrazolium bromide (MTT).
Incubate cells for an additional 3 hr.
At final time point, remove media from wells and replace with 120 μl of MTS working solution.
Incubate the MTS working solution with the cells for 3 hr.
Gently remove media from wells.
Add 100 μl of dimethylsulfoxide (Sigma) to each well.
Allow 10 min for MTT crystals to dissolve.
Transfer the solution to another well plate.
Move well contents to a new plate.
Read absorbance at 490 nm and determine percent viability by normalizing absorbance to the average absorbance of the pristine NiTi sample.
Seed rat aortic smooth muscle cells at 25,000 cells/chamber in an 8-chamber slide (Thermo Scientific).
Incubate cells for 3 days at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Fix cells on substrate with 4% formaldehyde in phosphate buffered saline for 20 min.
Permeabilize cells with 0.1% Triton-X for 1 min.
Mix 100 μl of alexafluor 488 phalloidin at 200 units/ml in methanol with 1.9 ml of phosphate buffered saline to make a solution.
Stain cells with 250 μl of the prepared alexafluor 488 phalloidin for 45 min.
Wash cells twice with phosphate buffered saline.
Mount nuclei with VectaShield fluorescent mounting medium containing DAPI (Vector Laboratories).
Collect confocal images using a Nikon Confocal TI.
Measure the dimensions of each substrate with calipers.
Take three measurements for each side of the approximately square samples.
Average the measurements to determine the length and width.
Incubate pristine NiTi, 1sccm Gr-NiTi, and 4sccm Gr-NiTi samples in PBS containing 1 mg/ml albumin at room temperature for 3 hr.
Incubate similar samples with PBS containing 1 mg/ml fibrinogen at room temperature for 3 hr.
Combine each sample with 200 μl of reducing sample buffer and boil for 5 min.
Dilute the samples in Tris/Glycine/SDS buffer.
Run the diluted samples through a 4-15% Tris polyacrylamide electrophoresis gel at 90 V for 100 min.
Stain the gel with SYPRO Red diluted at 1:5,000 in 7.5 v/v% acetic acid.
Incubate the gels with stained SYPRO Red solution for 60 min.
Image the stained gels using a Flourchem SP (Alpha Innotech).
Quantify fluorescent intensity from each sample using ImageJ software.
Normalize fluorescent intensity by the total area of substrate.
Compare fibrinogen adsorption to albumin adsorption.
Seed rat aortic smooth muscle cells at a density of 10,000 cells per substrate in a 96-well plate.
Grow cells for three days before removing media.
Extract total protein using RIPA buffer.
Quantify total protein using a standard BCA assay.
Dilute samples to the same concentration in RIPA.
Boil samples in reducing sample buffer for 5 minutes.
Separate proteins by electrophoresis on a 4-15% Tris polyacrylamide gel at 90 V for 100 minutes.
Transfer proteins to a PVDF membrane.
Block the membrane with a 1% non-fat dry milk solution.
Tag total actin with a rabbit anti-rat actin antibody.
Detect primary antibody using a BM chemiluminescent kit.
Image membranes using FlourChem SP imaging equipment.
Measure fluorescent intensity using ImageJ software.
Normalize fluorescent intensity by comparing to a pristine NiTi sample.
